title: SAJDAT AL-SAHW: HOW
bullets: In the final sitting, recite the tashahhud.
Give salam to the right according to the common Hanafi method.
Perform two sujuds, with takbir for each movement.
Sit again and recite tashahhud, Salawat Ibrahimiyya, and the final duʿā.
Finish with both salams.
note: Hanafi manuals transmit details in the method; follow your imam if he teaches a specific relied-upon form.
source: Hanafi fiqh; SeekersGuidance: How to Perform Sajda Sahu.

title: DOUBTS DURING SALAH
bullets: If a doubt is rare and you can make a reasonable judgment, act on what you think is most likely.
If you truly cannot decide, build on the lesser number and complete the prayer, then perform Sajdat al-Sahw where required.
Frequent obsessive doubt should not be fed; use the Hanafi rules your imam teaches for recurring waswasa.
source: Hanafi fiqh: doubt in prayer.

title: SAJDAT AL-TILAWAH
bullets: When a verse requiring prostration is recited or heard under the Hanafi conditions, one Sajdah al-Tilawah becomes wajib.
Outside prayer: say Allāhu akbar and prostrate once.
Say Allāhu akbar while rising.
No tashahhud and no closing salam are required.
The takbirs are Sunnah; do not raise the hands.
source: Hanafi fiqh; SeekersGuidance: Correct Method of Sajdat al-Tilawa.

title: FIVE DAILY FARD PRAYERS
bullets: FAJR
2 fard rakʿahs
DHUHR
4 fard rakʿahs
ASR
4 fard rakʿahs
MAGHRIB
3 fard rakʿahs
ISHA
4 fard rakʿahs
note: Hanafi Witr is wajib and is separate from the five daily fard prayers.
source: Established daily obligatory prayers.

title: 24-HOUR PRAYER MAP
bullets: NIGHT
Isha → Witr → Tahajjud/Qiyam; the final third is especially virtuous.
DAWN
Fajr Sunnah → Fajr fard.
MORNING
After sunrise restriction ends: Ishraq / Duha.
MIDDAY
Dhuhr Sunnah → Dhuhr fard → Dhuhr Sunnah.
AFTERNOON
Optional pre-Asr Sunnah → Asr fard.
SUNSET
Maghrib fard → Maghrib Sunnah → Awwabin.
EVENING
Optional pre-Isha prayer → Isha fard → Isha Sunnah → Witr.
source: Hanafi daily prayer structure.

title: WHEN THE FIVE PRAYER TIMES BEGIN
bullets: FAJR
Begins at true dawn; ends at sunrise.
DHUHR
Begins after the sun passes its zenith.
ASR
Hanafi relied-upon time begins when an object's shadow, excluding the noon shadow, reaches twice its length.
MAGHRIB
Begins immediately after sunset; ends when Isha enters.
ISHA
Begins after the relevant evening twilight disappears. Hanafi jurists record detail over the twilight criterion, so use a reliable Hanafi timetable for your location.
note: Local prayer timetables should be from a reliable source using Hanafi Asr if you are following the Hanafi school.
source: Hanafi prayer-time rules.

title: PROHIBITED + RESTRICTED TIMES
alert: DO NOT PRAY ANY RITUAL PRAYER DURING SUNRISE, ZAWAL, OR THE ACTUAL SUNSET WINDOW.
bullets: SUNRISE: from sunrise until the sun has clearly risen above the horizon.
ZAWAL: the brief period when the sun is at its zenith immediately before Dhuhr begins.
ACTUAL SUNSET: when the sun has weakened and is setting until it disappears.
After the fard Fajr until sunrise: do not offer nafl prayer.
After the fard Asr until sunset: do not offer nafl prayer.
Qada prayers are generally allowed after Fajr/Asr outside the three completely prohibited windows.
source: Hanafi fiqh; SeekersGuidance: prohibited times and makeup prayers.

title: FAJR: FULL HANAFI ROUTE
bullets: 2 rakʿahs Sunnah muʾakkadah before the fard.
2 rakʿahs fard.
When praying the fard alone, recite al-Fātiḥah plus another surah in both rakʿahs.
After rakʿah 2, complete the final sitting and taslim.
alert: AFTER THE FARD FAJR, DO NOT START NAFL PRAYER UNTIL THE SUNRISE RESTRICTION HAS ENDED.
source: Hanafi fiqh of the confirmed Sunnahs.

title: DHUHR: FULL HANAFI ROUTE
bullets: 4 rakʿahs Sunnah muʾakkadah before the fard.
4 rakʿahs fard.
2 rakʿahs Sunnah muʾakkadah after the fard.
In the fard when praying alone: al-Fātiḥah + surah in rakʿahs 1–2; al-Fātiḥah alone is the normal practice in rakʿahs 3–4.
First sitting after rakʿah 2: tashahhud only, then stand.
source: Hanafi fiqh of confirmed Sunnahs.

title: ASR: FULL HANAFI ROUTE
bullets: 4 rakʿahs fard.
A non-confirmed Sunnah prayer of 4 rakʿahs is recommended before the fard.
In the fard when praying alone: al-Fātiḥah + surah in rakʿahs 1–2; al-Fātiḥah alone is the normal practice in 3–4.
First sitting after rakʿah 2: tashahhud only, then stand.
alert: AFTER THE FARD ASR, DO NOT START NAFL PRAYER UNTIL SUNSET.
source: Hanafi fiqh of confirmed and non-confirmed Sunnahs.

title: MAGHRIB: FULL HANAFI ROUTE
bullets: 3 rakʿahs fard.
2 rakʿahs Sunnah muʾakkadah after the fard.
In the fard when praying alone: al-Fātiḥah + surah in rakʿahs 1–2.
Sit after rakʿah 2 for tashahhud, then stand.
Rakʿah 3: al-Fātiḥah alone is the normal Hanafi practice; then complete the final sitting.
source: Hanafi fiqh of Maghrib.

title: ISHA + WITR: HANAFI ROUTE
bullets: 4 rakʿahs fard Isha.
2 rakʿahs Sunnah muʾakkadah after the fard.
3 rakʿahs Witr, wajib in the Hanafi school.
A non-confirmed Sunnah prayer of 4 rakʿahs is recommended before Isha.
If you intend to pray Tahajjud later, you may delay Witr until the end of your night prayer if confident you will wake.
source: Hanafi fiqh of Isha and Witr.

title: WITR: THIRD RAKʿAH
bullets: After rakʿah 2, sit for tashahhud, then stand for the third rakʿah.
Recite al-Fātiḥah and another surah.
Then say Allāhu akbar while raising the hands to the earlobes.
Fold the hands again below the navel.
Recite the Qunut supplication.
Then go into ruku and finish the prayer normally.
source: Hanafi fiqh of Witr.

title: DUʿA AL-QUNUT • PART 1
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَسْتَعِينُكَ، وَنَسْتَغْفِرُكَ، وَنَسْتَهْدِيكَ، وَنُؤْمِنُ بِكَ، وَنَتُوبُ إِلَيْكَ، وَنَتَوَكَّلُ عَلَيْكَ، وَنُثْنِي عَلَيْكَ الْخَيْرَ كُلَّهُ، نَشْكُرُكَ وَلَا نَكْفُرُكَ، وَنَخْلَعُ وَنَتْرُكُ مَنْ يَفْجُرُكَ
translit: Allāhumma innā nastaʿīnuka wa nastaghfiruka wa nastahdīk, wa nuʾminu bika wa natūbu ilayk, wa natawakkalu ʿalayk, wa nuthnī ʿalayka l-khayra kullah, nashkuruka wa lā nakfuruk, wa nakhlaʿu wa natruku man yafjuruk.
meaning: O Allah, we seek Your help, forgiveness, and guidance; we believe in You, repent to You, rely on You, praise You for all good, thank You and do not deny You, and leave those who rebel against You.
source: Classical Hanafi Witr/Qunut texts.

title: DUʿA AL-QUNUT • PART 2
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ، وَلَكَ نُصَلِّي وَنَسْجُدُ، وَإِلَيْكَ نَسْعَى وَنَحْفِدُ، نَرْجُو رَحْمَتَكَ، وَنَخْشَى عَذَابَكَ، إِنَّ عَذَابَكَ بِالْكُفَّارِ مُلْحِقٌ
translit: Allāhumma iyyāka naʿbudu, wa laka nuṣallī wa nasjud, wa ilayka nasʿā wa naḥfid, narjū raḥmataka wa nakhshā ʿadhābak, inna ʿadhābaka bi-l-kuffāri mulḥiq.
meaning: O Allah, You alone we worship; for You we pray and prostrate; toward You we strive and hasten. We hope for Your mercy and fear Your punishment. Surely Your punishment overtakes the disbelievers.
note: Hanafi texts transmit accepted variants. Parts 1–2 together give one standard transmitted Hanafi form.
source: Classical Hanafi Witr/Qunut texts.

title: TAHAJJUD / NIGHT PRAYER
bullets: Pray after Isha and before Fajr.
Tahajjud especially refers to night prayer after having slept; Qiyam al-Layl is broader night worship.
Pray at least 2 rakʿahs; additional rakʿahs may be prayed in pairs.
The final third of the night is especially virtuous for prayer, Qur'an, istighfar, and duʿā.
source: Sahih Muslim 1163; last-third hadith in Bukhari/Muslim; Hanafi nafl fiqh.
reflection: “The best prayer after the obligatory prayer is the night prayer.”

title: LAST THIRD OF THE NIGHT
bullets: Use the period from Maghrib to Fajr as the night.
Find the total length of that period.
Divide it by 3.
The final third begins two-thirds of the way through the night and ends at Fajr.
EXAMPLE
If Maghrib is 6:00 PM and Fajr is 6:00 AM, the night is 12 hours; the last third is 2:00–6:00 AM.
source: Timing method derived from the hadith describing the last third of the night.

title: ISHRAQ / DUHA
bullets: Do not pray during the sunrise prohibition.
Once the sun has clearly risen, commonly about 15–20 minutes after sunrise, the Duha window begins.
Duha continues until shortly before zawal.
Minimum: 2 rakʿahs. Four is an excellent regular practice; more may be prayed.
Classical Hanafi texts generally treat Ishraq as the early portion of the Duha prayer window.
source: Hanafi fiqh of voluntary prayers and Duha.

title: AWWABIN AFTER MAGHRIB
bullets: After Maghrib, pray the 2 confirmed Sunnah rakʿahs.
A classical Hanafi recommended practice is to pray up to 6 rakʿahs after Maghrib; the 2 confirmed Sunnahs may be counted within the 6.
Pray them in sets of two.
Treat this as recommended worship, not fard or wajib.
source: Classical Hanafi voluntary-prayer discussions; reports on six rakʿahs after Maghrib.

title: SALAT AL-TAWBAH
bullets: Stop the sin and sincerely regret it.
If another person's rights were violated, restore the right or seek forgiveness as appropriate.
Make wudu well.
Pray 2 rakʿahs of voluntary prayer outside prohibited times.
Ask Allah sincerely for forgiveness and resolve not to return to the sin.
source: Sunan Abi Dawud 1521; Jamiʿ at-Tirmidhi 406; Hanafi repentance guidance.

title: ISTIKHARA: HOW TO PRAY
bullets: Use Istikhara for a permissible matter when you seek Allah’s guidance in choosing.
Pray 2 voluntary rakʿahs outside prohibited times.
After the prayer, praise Allah and send blessings on the Prophet ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam.
Recite the Istikhara duʿā, naming or holding the matter in mind at hādhā l-amr: 'this matter'.
Do not require a dream. Take sound counsel, make a decision, and trust Allah.
source: Sahih al-Bukhari 1166; Hanafi guidance on Istikhara.

title: ISTIKHARA DUʿA • PART 1
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْتَخِيرُكَ بِعِلْمِكَ، وَأَسْتَقْدِرُكَ بِقُدْرَتِكَ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ الْعَظِيمِ، فَإِنَّكَ تَقْدِرُ وَلَا أَقْدِرُ، وَتَعْلَمُ وَلَا أَعْلَمُ، وَأَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ
translit: Allāhumma innī astakhīruka biʿilmik, wa astaqdiruka biqudratik, wa asʾaluka min faḍlika l-ʿaẓīm. Fa-innaka taqdiru wa lā aqdir, wa taʿlamu wa lā aʿlam, wa Anta ʿAllāmu l-ghuyūb.
meaning: O Allah, I seek the better choice by Your knowledge, seek ability by Your power, and ask You from Your immense bounty. You are able and I am not; You know and I do not; You are the Knower of the unseen.
source: Sahih al-Bukhari 1166.

title: ISTIKHARA DUʿA • PART 2
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَذَا الْأَمْرَ خَيْرٌ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي، فَاقْدُرْهُ لِي وَيَسِّرْهُ لِي، ثُمَّ بَارِكْ لِي فِيهِ، وَإِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَذَا الْأَمْرَ شَرٌّ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي، فَاصْرِفْهُ عَنِّي وَاصْرِفْنِي عَنْهُ، وَاقْدُرْ لِيَ الْخَيْرَ حَيْثُ كَانَ، ثُمَّ أَرْضِنِي بِهِ
translit: Allāhumma in kunta taʿlamu anna hādhā l-amra khayrun lī fī dīnī wa maʿāshī wa ʿāqibati amrī, faqdurhu lī wa yassirhu lī, thumma bārik lī fīh. Wa in kunta taʿlamu anna hādhā l-amra sharrun lī fī dīnī wa maʿāshī wa ʿāqibati amrī, faṣrifhu ʿannī waṣrifnī ʿanhu, waqdur liya l-khayra ḥaythu kāna, thumma arḍinī bih.
meaning: If this matter is good for my religion, livelihood, and outcome, decree it for me, make it easy, and bless it. If it is bad for me, turn it away from me and me away from it; decree good for me wherever it is and make me content with it.
source: Sahih al-Bukhari 1166.

title: SALAT AL-HAJAH
bullets: Make wudu carefully.
Pray 2 voluntary rakʿahs outside prohibited times.
Praise Allah and send blessings upon the Prophet ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam.
Ask Allah sincerely for your need.
The well-known long Hajat supplication is reported with a weak chain; Hanafi jurists permit acting on such reports in virtues and also allow making any sound duʿā for the need.
source: Jamiʿ at-Tirmidhi 479 (weak report); Hanafi jurists on Salat al-Hajah.

title: SALAT AL-TASBIH
arabic: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَلَا إِلٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ
translit: Subḥāna llāh, wa-l-ḥamdu lillāh, wa lā ilāha illā llāh, wa-llāhu akbar.
meaning: Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no deity but Allah, and Allah is greater.
bullets: Four rakʿahs, with 75 repetitions of this tasbih in each rakʿah: 300 total.
The repetitions are distributed through standing, ruku, rising, and the two sujuds.
Many Hanafi jurists recommend this prayer; hadith scholars have differed over the strength of its reports.
source: Sunan Abi Dawud 1297 and related reports; classical Hanafi recommendation.
